objective: Memoize first-argument SameValueZero keys while preserving argument/result identities, cached falsy values and retryable throws.

relevanceRationale.transferable: Key identity, argument forwarding and error caching transfer widely.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The first-argument-only cache is deliberately bounded and explicit.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: NaN and undefined/falsy results are common sources of silent recomputation.

defects: Junior indexOf never found NaN keys, unlike the Map-based reference/senior.
Key equality, undefined/no-argument equivalence, result identity and synchronous-throw retry policy were implicit.
No upper-bound cache population/reuse check existed.
rationale: Replace parallel arrays/indexOf with a Map in junior; keep the correct reference/senior. Specify SameValueZero, object identity, first-key-only despite later arguments, forwarding original arguments on misses, exact cached values and uncached synchronous throws. Exclude receiver dependence/reentry and bound calls/arguments/string keys. State expected constant-cost wrapper Map work excluding fn, not an ECMAScript complexity guarantee. Add NaN, signed-zero key equivalence, distinct object/string/number keys, undefined result/no-argument key presence, original error retries and 500 distinct keys reused over 1000 calls.

objective: Assign fixed-five-letter green matches first and then left-to-right yellow matches without reusing answer positions.

relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: A word-game scoring rule is a clear applied counting problem.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Priority and limited resource consumption transfer beyond games.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Exactly five ASCII lowercase letters removes Unicode ambiguity.

defects: Senior used several map passes rather than the specified two indexed passes.
Junior appended a third for-of pass instead of directly joining its marks.
Lowercase letters did not explicitly distinguish fixed ASCII input from arbitrary Unicode letters.
rationale: Align senior to exactly two indexed passes and use join in junior. Explicitly retain fixed five ASCII a-z strings, including nondictionary inputs; the cost is constant for that fixed domain. Add an independent consumed-answer-position oracle covering all 1024 pairs of five-character binary-alphabet words. This finite exhaustive subdomain complements the existing other-letter examples and does not establish arbitrary-program correctness.

objective: Maintain separate bounded sliding acceptance queues with inclusive expiry, equal timestamps, zero limits and read-only remaining observations.

relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Bounded queue simulations illustrate real API behavior.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Expiry boundaries and accepted-versus-refused state transfer widely.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The exercise explicitly remains a small shift-based array implementation.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Equal timestamps, zero quota and remaining purity prevent boundary bugs.

defects: Numeric domains and nondecreasing-versus-strictly-increasing times were unspecified.
No sequence bound or explicit shift cost model was stated.
A limiter capped at 100 passed all old scenarios.
rationale: Retain all correct shift/push/while boards. State integer limit 0..1000, positive bounded window, nonnegative times through 10^12, nondecreasing including ties, independent factories and 10000 method calls. Explain conservative quadratic total sequence work with linear front moves and O(limit) queue space, not constant-time production rate limiting. Add 1000 same-time admissions, one refused request, all entries expiring at the exact boundary, repeated remaining calls, zero quota, upper timestamp/window boundary and 10000 one-slot expirations.

objective: Gather immutable reusable argument prefixes to stable JavaScript arity while preserving original values, results and errors.

relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Partial application is a useful functional API pattern.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Argument presence, immutable branching and arity transfer widely.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Bounded stable fn.length and receiver-independent functions scope the lesson.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Defaults/rest and shared mutable prefixes are important edge cases.

defects: The text incorrectly equated fn.length with every declared parameter.
Receiver, stable arity, opaque values/results/errors and branch bounds were unspecified.
A clone-before-callback variant passed value-only old checks.
rationale: Retain all correct supplied algorithms. Correct fn.length for defaults/rest and state stable arity 0..100, no receiver reliance, up to 100 branch calls/1000 gathered arguments, empty stages, exact ordered values/results and unchanged errors. Explain linear per-gather copying with potentially quadratic aggregate copies, excluding fn work. Add opaque object/array/undefined preservation, exact result identity, defaults/rest and zero arity, repeated throw identity and 1000 original arguments delivered in one qualifying call.

objective: Return fresh cumulative scores for the scorable prefix of a legal fixed ten-frame bowling game.

relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: A scorecard is a concrete state-machine exercise.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Lookahead without consuming bonuses transfers to parsers.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Valid prefixes isolate scoring from game validation.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Tenth-frame and incomplete-bonus handling prevent extra frames.

defects: Junior omitted the requested small rule helpers.
Valid game prefix, integer pins, read-only input and fresh output were implicit.
Fixed ten-frame complexity was not explained.
rationale: Add hasRoll/isStrike/isSpare helpers to junior without changing the scoring algorithm. Define a valid dense read-only prefix of one standard game, at most 21 integer rolls including legal tenth bonuses, invalid games outside scope, fresh outputs and constant fixed-game work/space. Add repeated output freshness, unchanged original rolls and tenth-frame strike awaiting zero/one/two bonus rolls. Verify rule wording against USBC scoring material; preserve all existing strike/spare/mixed examples.
